stem: A tower stands vertically on the ground. From a point on the ground, which is 15 m away from the foot of the tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is found to be \(60^\circ\). Find the height of the tower.
solution:
Let AB represent the tower, CB the distance of the point from the tower, and \(\angle\)ACB the angle of elevation. Triangle ACB is right-angled at B.

To solve, we choose the trigonometric ratio involving AB (what we want) and CB (what we know) — that is the tangent:

\(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{\text{AB}}{\text{CB}}\)

i.e., \(\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{\text{AB}}{15}\)

i.e., \(\text{AB} = 15\sqrt{3}\)

Hence, the height of the tower is \(15\sqrt{3}\) m.

stem: An electrician has to repair an electric fault on a pole of height 5 m. She needs to reach a point 1.3 m below the top of the pole to undertake the repair work. What should be the length of the ladder that she should use which, when inclined at an angle of \(60^\circ\) to the horizontal, would enable her to reach the required position? Also, how far from the foot of the pole should she place the foot of the ladder? (You may take \(\sqrt{3} = 1.73\))
solution:
Let AD be the pole and BD the part she must reach. Then

\(\text{BD} = \text{AD} - \text{AB} = (5 - 1.3)\) m \(= 3.7\) m.

Here BC represents the ladder. We need to find its length BC and the distance DC of its foot from the pole.

\(\dfrac{\text{BD}}{\text{BC}} = \sin 60^\circ\), i.e., \(\dfrac{3.7}{\text{BC}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\)

Therefore, \(\text{BC} = \dfrac{3.7 \times 2}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{7.4}{1.73} = 4.28\) m (approx.).

\(\dfrac{\text{DC}}{\text{BD}} = \cot 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), i.e., \(\text{DC} = \dfrac{3.7}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{3.7}{1.73} = 2.14\) m (approx.).

So she should use a ladder about 4.28 m long, placing its foot about 2.14 m from the pole.

stem: An observer 1.5 m tall is 28.5 m away from a chimney. The angle of elevation of the top of the chimney from her eyes is \(45^\circ\). What is the height of the chimney?
solution:
Let AB be the chimney, CD the observer and \(\angle\)ADE the angle of elevation. Triangle ADE is right-angled at E.

Here \(\text{AB} = \text{AE} + \text{BE}\), where \(\text{BE} = \text{CD} = 1.5\) m and \(\text{DE} = \text{CB} = 28.5\) m.

\(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{\text{AE}}{\text{DE}} = \dfrac{\text{AE}}{28.5}\)

i.e., \(1 = \dfrac{\text{AE}}{28.5}\), so \(\text{AE} = 28.5\) m.

So the height of the chimney \(= \text{AE} + \text{BE} = 28.5 + 1.5 = 30\) m.

stem: From a point P on the ground the angle of elevation of the top of a 10 m tall building is \(30^\circ\). A flag is hoisted at the top of the building and the angle of elevation of the top of the flagstaff from P is \(45^\circ\). Find the length of the flagstaff and the distance of the building from the point P. (You may take \(\sqrt{3} = 1.732\))
solution:
Let AB denote the height of the building, BD the flagstaff and P the given point. There are two right triangles PAB and PAD.

In right \(\triangle\)PAB, \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{\text{AB}}{\text{AP}}\),

i.e., \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{10}{\text{AP}}\), so \(\text{AP} = 10\sqrt{3} = 17.32\) m.

In right \(\triangle\)PAD, \(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{\text{AD}}{\text{AP}}\),

i.e., \(1 = \dfrac{\text{AD}}{10\sqrt{3}}\), so \(\text{AD} = 10\sqrt{3}\) m.

Therefore, the length of the flagstaff \(= \text{BD} = \text{AD} - \text{AB} = 10\sqrt{3} - 10 = 10(\sqrt{3} - 1) = 7.32\) m.

And the distance of the building from P is \(17.32\) m.

stem: The shadow of a tower standing on a level ground is found to be 40 m longer when the Sun’s altitude is \(30^\circ\) than when it is \(60^\circ\). Find the height of the tower.
solution:
Let AB be the tower and BC the length of the shadow when the Sun’s altitude is \(60^\circ\); let DB be the shadow when the altitude is \(30^\circ\).

Then \(\text{DC} = 40\) m, and let \(\text{AB} = h\) m and \(\text{BC} = x\) m.

In right \(\triangle\)ABC, \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{h}{x}\), so \(x = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}}\).  ... (1)

In right \(\triangle\)ABD, \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{h}{x + 40}\), so \(x + 40 = h\sqrt{3}\).  ... (2)

Substituting (1) into (2): \(\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}} + 40 = h\sqrt{3}\),

i.e., \(h + 40\sqrt{3} = 3h\), i.e., \(2h = 40\sqrt{3}\), so \(h = 20\sqrt{3}\).

So the height of the tower is \(20\sqrt{3}\) m.

stem: The angles of depression of the top and the bottom of an 8 m tall building from the top of a multi-storeyed building are \(30^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\), respectively. Find the height of the multi-storeyed building and the distance between the two buildings.
solution:
Let PC denote the multi-storeyed building and AB the 8 m tall building. Let the distance between them be \(d\) and the height of the multi-storeyed building be \(h\).

The angle of depression of the BOTTOM of AB is \(45^\circ\), so in that right triangle

\(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{h}{d}\), giving \(h = d\).  ... (1)

The angle of depression of the TOP of AB is \(30^\circ\). The vertical drop to that top is \(h - 8\), so

\(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{h - 8}{d}\), giving \(h - 8 = \dfrac{d}{\sqrt{3}}\).  ... (2)

Substituting \(h = d\) into (2): \(d - 8 = \dfrac{d}{\sqrt{3}}\),

i.e., \(d\sqrt{3} - 8\sqrt{3} = d\), i.e., \(d(\sqrt{3} - 1) = 8\sqrt{3}\),

so \(d = \dfrac{8\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3} - 1} = \dfrac{8\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{2} = 4\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3} + 1) = 4(3 + \sqrt{3})\).

So the height of the multi-storeyed building is \(4(3 + \sqrt{3})\) m and the distance between the two buildings is also \(4(3 + \sqrt{3})\) m.

stem: From a point on a bridge across a river, the angles of depression of the banks on opposite sides of the river are \(30^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\), respectively. If the bridge is at a height of 3 m from the banks, find the width of the river.
solution:
Let A and B represent points on the banks on opposite sides of the river, so AB is the width of the river. Let P be the point on the bridge, with D the foot of the perpendicular from P, so \(\text{DP} = 3\) m.

In right \(\triangle\)PAD, \(\angle\)A \(= 30^\circ\), so

\(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{\text{PD}}{\text{AD}}\), i.e., \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{3}{\text{AD}}\), so \(\text{AD} = 3\sqrt{3}\) m.

In right \(\triangle\)PBD, \(\angle\)B \(= 45^\circ\), so \(\text{BD} = \text{PD} = 3\) m.

Now \(\text{AB} = \text{BD} + \text{AD} = 3 + 3\sqrt{3} = 3(1 + \sqrt{3})\) m.

Therefore, the width of the river is \(3(\sqrt{3} + 1)\) m.

stem: A circus artist is climbing a 20 m long rope, which is tightly stretched and tied from the top of a vertical pole to the ground. Find the height of the pole, if the angle made by the rope with the ground level is \(30^\circ\) (see Fig. 9.11).
solution:
Let AB be the pole and AC the rope, with \(\angle\)ACB \(= 30^\circ\) and \(\text{AC} = 20\) m.

\(\sin 30^\circ = \dfrac{\text{AB}}{\text{AC}}\), i.e., \(\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{\text{AB}}{20}\).

So \(\text{AB} = 10\) m — the height of the pole is **10 m**.

stem: A tree breaks due to storm and the broken part bends so that the top of the tree touches the ground making an angle \(30^\circ\) with it. The distance between the foot of the tree to the point where the top touches the ground is 8 m. Find the height of the tree.
solution:
Let AB be the part still standing and BC the broken part, now leaning to touch the ground at C with \(\angle\)ACB \(= 30^\circ\) and \(\text{AC} = 8\) m.

\(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{\text{AB}}{\text{AC}}\), so \(\text{AB} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{3}}\) m.

\(\cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{\text{AC}}{\text{BC}}\), so \(\text{BC} = \dfrac{8}{\cos 30^\circ} = \dfrac{16}{\sqrt{3}}\) m.

The original height of the tree is \(\text{AB} + \text{BC} = \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{3}} + \dfrac{16}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{24}{\sqrt{3}} = 8\sqrt{3}\) m.

stem: A contractor plans to install two slides for the children to play in a park. For the children below the age of 5 years, she prefers to have a slide whose top is at a height of 1.5 m, and is inclined at an angle of \(30^\circ\) to the ground, whereas for elder children, she wants to have a steep slide at a height of 3 m, and inclined at an angle of \(60^\circ\) to the ground. What should be the length of the slide in each case?
solution:
In each case the slide is the hypotenuse and the given height is the opposite side, so \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{\text{height}}{\text{length}}\).

**Younger children:** \(\sin 30^\circ = \dfrac{1.5}{L}\), i.e., \(\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1.5}{L}\), so \(L = 3\) m.

**Elder children:** \(\sin 60^\circ = \dfrac{3}{L}\), i.e., \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \dfrac{3}{L}\), so \(L = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{3}} = 2\sqrt{3}\) m.

stem: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground, which is 30 m away from the foot of the tower, is \(30^\circ\). Find the height of the tower.
solution:
\(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{h}{30}\), i.e., \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{h}{30}\).

So \(h = \dfrac{30}{\sqrt{3}} = 10\sqrt{3}\) m.

stem: A kite is flying at a height of 60 m above the ground. The string attached to the kite is temporarily tied to a point on the ground. The inclination of the string with the ground is \(60^\circ\). Find the length of the string, assuming that there is no slack in the string.
solution:
\(\sin 60^\circ = \dfrac{60}{L}\), i.e., \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \dfrac{60}{L}\).

So \(L = \dfrac{120}{\sqrt{3}} = 40\sqrt{3}\) m.

stem: A 1.5 m tall boy is standing at some distance from a 30 m tall building. The angle of elevation from his eyes to the top of the building increases from \(30^\circ\) to \(60^\circ\) as he walks towards the building. Find the distance he walked towards the building.
solution:
The boy’s eyes are 1.5 m above the ground, so the effective height of the building above eye level is \(30 - 1.5 = 28.5\) m.

At \(30^\circ\): \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{28.5}{d_1}\), so \(d_1 = 28.5\sqrt{3}\) m.

At \(60^\circ\): \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{28.5}{d_2}\), so \(d_2 = \dfrac{28.5}{\sqrt{3}}\) m.

Distance walked \(= d_1 - d_2 = 28.5\sqrt{3} - \dfrac{28.5}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{28.5(3 - 1)}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{57}{\sqrt{3}} = 19\sqrt{3}\) m.

stem: From a point on the ground, the angles of elevation of the bottom and the top of a transmission tower fixed at the top of a 20 m high building are \(45^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\) respectively. Find the height of the tower.
solution:
The bottom of the tower is the top of the 20 m building. At \(45^\circ\):

\(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{20}{d}\), so \(d = 20\) m.

At \(60^\circ\) the total height (building \(+\) tower) satisfies

\(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{20 + h}{20}\), i.e., \(20 + h = 20\sqrt{3}\).

So \(h = 20\sqrt{3} - 20 = 20(\sqrt{3} - 1)\) m.

stem: A statue, 1.6 m tall, stands on the top of a pedestal. From a point on the ground, the angle of elevation of the top of the statue is \(60^\circ\) and from the same point the angle of elevation of the top of the pedestal is \(45^\circ\). Find the height of the pedestal.
solution:
Let the pedestal be \(h\) m tall and the point be \(d\) m from its foot.

At \(45^\circ\) (top of pedestal): \(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{h}{d}\), so \(d = h\).

At \(60^\circ\) (top of statue): \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{h + 1.6}{d} = \dfrac{h + 1.6}{h}\).

So \(h\sqrt{3} = h + 1.6\), i.e., \(h(\sqrt{3} - 1) = 1.6\),

\(h = \dfrac{1.6}{\sqrt{3} - 1} = \dfrac{1.6(\sqrt{3} + 1)}{2} = 0.8(\sqrt{3} + 1)\) m.

stem: The angle of elevation of the top of a building from the foot of the tower is \(30^\circ\) and the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from the foot of the building is \(60^\circ\). If the tower is 50 m high, find the height of the building.
solution:
Let the distance between the foot of the building and the foot of the tower be \(d\).

From the foot of the BUILDING, the tower subtends \(60^\circ\):

\(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{50}{d}\), so \(d = \dfrac{50}{\sqrt{3}}\) m.

From the foot of the TOWER, the building subtends \(30^\circ\):

\(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{h}{d}\), so \(h = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \times \dfrac{50}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{50}{3} = 16\dfrac{2}{3}\) m.

stem: Two poles of equal heights are standing opposite each other on either side of the road, which is 80 m wide. From a point between them on the road, the angles of elevation of the top of the poles are \(60^\circ\) and \(30^\circ\), respectively. Find the height of the poles and the distances of the point from the poles.
solution:
Let the point be \(x\) m from the first pole and \(y\) m from the second, with \(x + y = 80\), and let each pole be \(h\) m tall.

\(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{h}{x}\) gives \(h = x\sqrt{3}\).

\(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{h}{y}\) gives \(h = \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{3}}\).

Equating: \(x\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{3}}\), i.e., \(3x = y\).

With \(x + y = 80\): \(4x = 80\), so \(x = 20\) m and \(y = 60\) m.

Then \(h = 20\sqrt{3}\) m.

So the poles are \(20\sqrt{3}\) m high, and the point is 20 m from one pole and 60 m from the other.

stem: A TV tower stands vertically on a bank of a canal. From a point on the other bank directly opposite the tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is \(60^\circ\). From another point 20 m away from this point on the line joining this point to the foot of the tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is \(30^\circ\) (see Fig. 9.12). Find the height of the tower and the width of the canal.
solution:
Let the width of the canal be \(d\) m and the height of the tower \(h\) m.

At \(60^\circ\): \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{h}{d}\), so \(h = d\sqrt{3}\).

At \(30^\circ\), from 20 m further back: \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{h}{d + 20}\), so \(h\sqrt{3} = d + 20\).

Substituting: \(d \times 3 = d + 20\), i.e., \(2d = 20\), so \(d = 10\) m.

Then \(h = 10\sqrt{3}\) m.

So the tower is \(10\sqrt{3}\) m high and the canal is 10 m wide.

stem: From the top of a 7 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a cable tower is \(60^\circ\) and the angle of depression of its foot is \(45^\circ\). Determine the height of the tower.
solution:
Let the horizontal distance between the building and the tower be \(d\).

The angle of DEPRESSION of the tower’s foot is \(45^\circ\), and the drop is the building’s height:

\(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{7}{d}\), so \(d = 7\) m.

The angle of ELEVATION of the tower’s top is \(60^\circ\), measured from the top of the building, so the rise above the building is

\(7\tan 60^\circ = 7\sqrt{3}\) m.

Total height of the tower \(= 7 + 7\sqrt{3} = 7(\sqrt{3} + 1)\) m.

stem: As observed from the top of a 75 m high lighthouse from the sea-level, the angles of depression of two ships are \(30^\circ\) and \(45^\circ\). If one ship is exactly behind the other on the same side of the lighthouse, find the distance between the two ships.
solution:
The nearer ship has the LARGER depression angle.

At \(45^\circ\): \(\tan 45^\circ = \dfrac{75}{d_1}\), so \(d_1 = 75\) m.

At \(30^\circ\): \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{75}{d_2}\), so \(d_2 = 75\sqrt{3}\) m.

Distance between the ships \(= d_2 - d_1 = 75\sqrt{3} - 75 = 75(\sqrt{3} - 1)\) m.

stem: A 1.2 m tall girl spots a balloon moving with the wind in a horizontal line at a height of 88.2 m from the ground. The angle of elevation of the balloon from the eyes of the girl at any instant is \(60^\circ\). After some time, the angle of elevation reduces to \(30^\circ\) (see Fig. 9.13). Find the distance travelled by the balloon during the interval.
solution:
The girl’s eyes are 1.2 m above the ground, so the balloon is \(88.2 - 1.2 = 87\) m above eye level.

At \(60^\circ\): \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{87}{d_1}\), so \(d_1 = \dfrac{87}{\sqrt{3}} = 29\sqrt{3}\) m.

At \(30^\circ\): \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{87}{d_2}\), so \(d_2 = 87\sqrt{3}\) m.

Distance travelled \(= d_2 - d_1 = 87\sqrt{3} - 29\sqrt{3} = 58\sqrt{3}\) m.

stem: A straight highway leads to the foot of a tower. A man standing at the top of the tower observes a car at an angle of depression of \(30^\circ\), which is approaching the foot of the tower with a uniform speed. Six seconds later, the angle of depression of the car is found to be \(60^\circ\). Find the time taken by the car to reach the foot of the tower from this point.
solution:
Let the tower be \(h\) m high.

At the first sighting (\(30^\circ\)): distance from the foot \(= \dfrac{h}{\tan 30^\circ} = h\sqrt{3}\).

Six seconds later (\(60^\circ\)): distance \(= \dfrac{h}{\tan 60^\circ} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}}\).

So in 6 seconds the car covers \(h\sqrt{3} - \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{h(3 - 1)}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{2h}{\sqrt{3}}\).

The remaining distance is \(\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{3}}\), which is exactly HALF of what was just covered.

Since the speed is uniform, the remaining time is \(\dfrac{6}{2} = 3\) seconds.
